model.rationale: Thompson combines a comfortable district lean, decades of incumbency, and a roughly 35-to-1 cash advantage over Ron Eller, with no outside spending against him. Markets price this near 97% Democratic, matching what the fundamentals alone would suggest.
model.watch: Only a major national wave against Democrats or an unexpected scandal involving Thompson could narrow this race, and no current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Mississippi's 2nd District leans Democratic by about eleven points, and Bennie Thompson has held the seat since 1993. He enters the general election with a large financial advantage: roughly $1.36 million on hand after raising about $928,000, against Republican Ron Eller's $38,000. No outside groups have spent against Thompson, and an independent candidate trails far behind in resources.

Prediction markets put Thompson's chances near 97 percent, and no general-election polls or expert ratings contest that picture. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and money — all point the same direction, making this one of the safest Democratic House seats on the ballot. The main uncertainty is the absence of local polling, which leaves some room for error around the expected margin but little realistic chance of an upset.
